name: Machilipatnam (Pedana) block-printed Kalamkari
summary: Machilipatnam Kalamkari is a hand-block-printed cotton textile tradition from Pedana and neighbouring villages near Machilipatnam (Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh), registered as a Geographical Indication (application no. 90; certificate 2008). Cloth is bleached, treated with myrobalan, block-printed with iron (kasim) and alum (karam) mordants, boiled in alizarin with plant additives, overprinted with yellow and indigo, and fixed through repeated washing in flowing water and sun-drying. The tradition descends from the Golconda-era port trade in Masulipatnam painted and printed cottons for Persia and Europe, where blocks progressively replaced the hand-drawn kalam.
